hook.line: At seventy-one, Don Hernando still carried sacks of coffee up the stairs. Tomás wants to say so in the newsletter, and Spanish has a ready-made picture for it.
hook.es: Don Hernando era fuerte como un roble.
hook.en: Don Hernando was as strong as an oak.

examples.es: Mi abuelo es fuerte como un roble.
examples.en: My grandad is as strong as an oak.

examples.es: Este pan está duro como una piedra.
examples.en: This bread is as hard as a rock.

examples.es: Esta maleta es pesada como el plomo.
examples.en: This suitcase is as heavy as lead.

examples.es: A los setenta y un años, Don Hernando era fuerte como un roble.
examples.en: At seventy-one, Don Hernando was as strong as an oak.

examples.es: Simón es ligero como una pluma.

examples.es: Mariana es rápida como un rayo.
examples.en: Mariana is as quick as lightning.

rule:
Spanish loves a fixed comparison: *adjective + como + a thing*.

*Fuerte como un roble* (strong as an oak). *Duro como una piedra* (hard as a rock). *Pesado como el plomo* (heavy as lead). *Ligero como una pluma* (light as a feather).

The thing is fixed. Do not swap it: nobody says "fuerte como un pino".

The adjective agrees with who you describe: *Ella es rápida como un rayo.* The thing after *como* never changes.

Some match English, some do not: where English says "strong as an ox", Spanish says "strong as an oak".
smallPrint: Teachers call these fixed similes (*comparaciones fijas*).

readAndPick.es: Mi abuelo es fuerte como un roble.
options: My grandad is as strong as an oak.
My grandad is as weak as a leaf.
My grandad is taller than an oak.

readAndPick.es: Este pan está duro como una piedra.
options: This bread is as soft as a pillow.
This bread is as hard as a rock.
This bread is shaped like a rock.

readAndPick.es: Esta maleta es pesada como el plomo.
options: This suitcase is as light as a feather.
This suitcase is made of plastic.
This suitcase is as heavy as lead.

readAndPick.es: Simón es ligero como una pluma.
options: Simón is as light as a feather.
Simón is as heavy as lead.
Simón is as hard as a rock.

readAndPick.es: Mariana es rápida como un rayo.
options: Mariana is as slow as a snail.
Mariana is as quick as lightning.
Mariana is as tall as a tower.

readAndPick.es: El pastel quedó duro como una piedra.
options: The cake came out soft as a cloud.
The cake came out heavy as lead.
The cake came out hard as a rock.

readAndPick.es: Rosa era fuerte como un roble.
options: Rosa was as strong as an oak.
Rosa is as strong as an oak.
Rosa will be as strong as an oak.

readAndPick.es: Tomás se quedó callado como una tumba.
options: Tomás shouted like a storm.
Tomás stayed as quiet as a grave.
Tomás stood as still as a statue.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *un roble* or *una piedra*: Mi abuelo es fuerte como ___. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Mi abuelo es fuerte como un roble.
yourTurn.why: Strong people are compared to *un roble*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *una piedra* or *una pluma*: Este pan está duro como ___. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Este pan está duro como una piedra.
yourTurn.why: Hard goes with *una piedra*; *una pluma* is for light things.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: "This suitcase is as heavy as lead."
yourTurn.answer: Esta maleta es pesada como el plomo.
accept: Esta maleta es tan pesada como el plomo.
yourTurn.why: *Pesada* agrees with *maleta*, and *como el plomo* stays fixed.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: "Mariana is as quick as lightning."
yourTurn.answer: Mariana es rápida como un rayo.
accept: Mariana es tan rápida como un rayo.
yourTurn.why: Feminine *rápida* for Mariana, and the thing after *como* does not change.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: "Simón is as light as a feather."
yourTurn.answer: Simón es ligero como una pluma.
accept: Simón es tan ligero como una pluma.
Simón es liviano como una pluma.
yourTurn.why: *Ligero* is masculine for Simón, and *una pluma* is the fixed picture.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about your grandmother: *Mi abuelo es fuerte como un roble.* Say "My grandmother is as strong as an oak."
yourTurn.answer: Mi abuela es fuerte como un roble.
accept: Mi abuela es tan fuerte como un roble.
yourTurn.why: *Fuerte* has one form for both, and *un roble* stays the same.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it the past: *Rosa es fuerte como un roble.* Say "Rosa was as strong as an oak."
yourTurn.answer: Rosa era fuerte como un roble.
accept: Rosa era tan fuerte como un roble.

pitfalls.wrong: Mi abuelo es fuerte como un pino.
pitfalls.right: Mi abuelo es fuerte como un roble.
pitfalls.why: Almost. These comparisons are fixed, so keep the standard picture: the oak.

pitfalls.wrong: Este pan es duro como una piedra.
pitfalls.right: Este pan está duro como una piedra.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The bread got hard, it was not born hard, so Spanish uses *está*.

pitfalls.wrong: Mariana es rápido como un rayo.
pitfalls.right: Mariana es rápida como un rayo.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The adjective agrees with Mariana, so it is feminine: *rápida*.

personal: Describe someone you know with one fixed comparison, for example *fuerte como un roble* or *rápido como un rayo*.
